newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece to campaign for Cyprus missile purchase.
newsitem.headline: Greece to campaign for Cyprus missile purchase.

text.p: Greece vowed on Tuesday to campaign internationally to ensure that Cyprus can proceed with the purchase of a Russian anti-aircraft missile defence system despite objections by Ankara, Washington and London.

"Cyprus is an independent country that has every right to apply defence programmes," a foreign ministry statement said. "Greece will use all means at its disposal with international bodies and friendly governments so that Ankara's efforts (to cancel the deal) do not succeed."

Turkey said on Monday it would not accept a change in the balance of power on the divided island of Cyprus as a result of the Cypriot government's decision to buy the surface-to-air missiles, but did not say what measures it would take.

Turkey has occupied northern Cyprus since an invasion in 1974 in response to a short-lived coup engineered by a military justa then ruling Greece. The island's division remains a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey.
United Nations efforts to re-unite the two communities in a federation have so far failed.
The United States has criticised the purchase, saying it would introduce a new and destabilising element and undermine peace moves. Britain also expressed concern.
But Cyprus shrugged off the criticism as unfair, saying the system was essential to defend Greek Cypriots on the island and rejecting what it said was a double standard.

"Similar criticism has never been raised against the presence of 35,000 Turkish troops illegally in Cyprus who are armed with American weapons...NATO weapons destined to be used against NATO enemies," Cypriot government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters.
Purchase of Russia's S-300 system, with a 90-mile (145-km) range, is the Cypriot government's first step toward building a credible air defence system.

The United Nations have described Cyprus as one of the most heavily militarised areas in the world. Four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot have been killed along the UN-guarded buffer zone in recent months, in the worst tension on the island since 1974.
